signal: Artisan announced general availability of Ava 2.0, its rebuilt AI BDR, now self-serve

email.body1:
Walker, saw Artisan ship Ava 2.0 GA and open it up self-serve.

A self-serve launch usually floods the top of funnel with more accounts than the human team can cover and follow up on, and that is where pipeline goes cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously alongside your reps, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Artisan off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Walker, quick follow-up for Artisan.

With a self-serve motion live, the pipeline target moves faster than headcount can. Most sales leaders don't actually know how many meetings the team needs to book to hit the new number, so the gap shows up late.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Artisan needs to close that gap this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Walker, last bit of proof for Artisan.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Artisan's reply rate likely compares to other growth-stage GTM startups. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through it?
email.body4:
Walker, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling your own outbound without adding headcount isn't a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Launching self-serve is its own kind of busy.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your motion? I'll tailor it to Artisan either way.
